newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: "Mr Clean" named S.Korean ruling party chief--TV.
newsitem.headline: "Mr Clean" named S.Korean ruling party chief--TV.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam has named former supreme court judge Lee Hoi-chang as chairman of his ruling New Korea Party, state television reported on Thursday.

Lee, dubbed "Mr Clean" by the local media, has a reputation for refusing to compromise his principles. Kim apparently turned to the independent-minded Lee in hopes of restoring his political credibility, badly damaged by a loans scandal.

Lee has recently urged the government to reinvestigate the bribes-for-loans scandal involving the failed Hanbo Steel Co. The scandal has already landed three of Kim's close associates behind bars on bribery charges.
Lee was once prime minister under Kim but quit the post in 1994 over the level of power he could exercise.
He is one of nine party leaders tipped as contenders for the party's nomination as presidential candidate in elections in December.
Kim is barred by the constitution from seeking a second term, but political analysts say he will try to work behind the scenes to put in place a successor.
